reachable: Yes, at the scored position and with gradient. (1) The optimizer is not a mechanism the model reads — it changes the weights the probe evaluates, and it demonstrably does: training the real genome end-to-end through H._train for 120 steps with the new optim vs the parent optim gives max|new - parent| = 0.0349 over the final weights, and repeated identical runs are bit-identical. (2) The one correctness property the mechanism hangs on — that evaluation runs on undisplaced weights — is enforced by construction and verified three ways: in a toy loop, in a 400-step real-net loop, and inside the actual harness (`taken == total_steps == 120/300`, `len(opt.shift.displacement) == 0` at return). The harness loop is exactly `for step in range(1, steps+1)` with `steps` the same integer passed to `make`, and the only early exit (`not torch.isfinite(loss)`) returns ok=False, which the adapter turns into `train_diverged` rather than scoring, so no path scores displaced weights. (3) The head the crossover brings in is live at the scored read position: on the instrument's odd [cmd, obs, ..., cmd] layout, toggling copy_transport.out_scale from 0 to 0.1 moves the prediction at rpos by 0.40-0.51, and backward from the read position alone gives nonzero grad to out_scale (2.04), copy_transport.addr.weight (0.558), cmd_feat.weight (0.940) — the head's query is built from `cf = gelu(cmd_feat(c))` with `read_ok = live[:, 0::2]`, no observation term, exactly as the hypothesis states.
solves_outside_model: No. The optim axis never touches model inputs — it only reads p.grad and writes p.data. The batcher r2 parses command strings with a symbolic mv/cp/redirect tracker, but it only builds buckets keyed by (image, normalised path, hop count) and returns a list of integer indices; it never mutates the `fit` sequence dicts it is handed, and the harness validates only length/bounds on what it returns. That is sample selection, which the brief permits. The r3 head's read path is built from the token embeddings the model already sees (`cmd_feat` on tok[:, 0::2]) with no side channel. Nothing resolved reaches the model's input at scoring time.
summary: The new optimizer code does what its equation says, verified by execution. eps_t = rho_t * (T^2 m)/||T m|| with T = |theta|+eta and m an EMA of the clipped gradient is exactly what `_AdaptiveSharpnessShift.displace` computes; `revert()` is unconditional at the top of every step so AdamW/Muon/decay/cap all act on the base point; the displacement is skipped on the final step so evaluation runs undisplaced (confirmed inside the real harness); the ramp is zero through `warm` then smoothsteps to rho over `sharp_ramp_frac*steps`; and with rho=0 the file is bit-identical to the parent optimizer (max|delta| = 0.0 over 60 steps). The Muon sibling rule behaves as claimed — r3's copy_transport.addr (64,128) is a lone shape and goes to AdamW while addr_src/addr_dst (64,256) pair and route.  What does NOT hold is the mechanism story. Traced inside real training on the cups pack, 98-99.9% of the perturbation energy from ~step 90 onward lands on a single scalar, the r3 head's `copy_transport.log_temp`, jittering the retrieval temperature by ~2.3x every step; the r23 routing gates and addressing matrices the hypothesis argues the mechanism robustifies receive relative perturbations of 1e-5 to 1e-3. So what gets scored is not "sharpness-aware training of the gate landscape", it is a large consistent-direction ascent step on one head temperature scalar plus a numerically negligible perturbation of everything else. This is faithful ASAM arithmetic — the T^2 weighting plus one global normalization over 5.67M parameters concentrates the whole budget on whichever few large-|theta|, large-gradient scalars exist, and nothing excludes norms/biases/temperatures — but it is not the mechanism the hypothesis describes, and the author's own "INTERACTIONS I CHECKED BY HAND" section checked Muon routing and cap targets while missing where the perturbation budget actually goes. Three smaller claims are also wrong: the cap set is three (768,768) tensors not one, the r18->r3 head swap is not a strict superset (r23 does expose transition_from_emb, so the parent's head was live, and r3's supervision of it uses a different miner and weights), and the added optimizer cost is ~2 host syncs per parameter tensor and a measured 3x optimizer-step slowdown, not "one scalar sync".

divergences.claim: "WHY THIS SHOULD MOVE THE MEASURED QUANTITY … the r23 arch routes content through a bank of sigmoid gates (move/write/erase, plus the alpha and tp_gate blend) … A flat minimum is one where the same gate decision survives a |theta|-relative perturbation of the weights" and "the perturbation lands almost entirely on the trunk … it means the mechanism regularises the trunk more than the readout."
divergences.what_the_code_does: Measured inside the real harness loop on the real cups pack (2304 train seqs, bs=16, 300 steps, CPU): from roughly step 90 onward, 98-99.9% of the squared perturbation energy sits on ONE scalar — `copy_transport.log_temp`, the r3 head's retrieval softmax temperature. ||eps|| ~= 0.857 of which |eps| on log_temp alone is 0.853, against a base value of ~-1.71, i.e. the head's retrieval temperature is multiplied/divided by e^0.85 ~= 2.3x on every post-warmup step. The routing parameters the hypothesis argues about get essentially nothing: addr_src.weight share 2.3e-6 (relative perturbation 2.8e-4), addr_dst.weight 3.6e-6 (3.6e-4), tp_out.weight 5.3e-8 (2.6e-5), tp_gate.bias 1e-4, x_gate.bias 6e-4, copy_transport.addr.weight 3.7e-7. This is structural, not incidental: ASAM's T^2 = (|theta|+eta)^2 weighting combined with a single GLOBAL normalization over 5.67M parameters lets whichever few high-|theta|, high-gradient SCALARS exist absorb the whole perturbation budget, and nothing here excludes norms/biases/temperatures the way SAM/ASAM implementations usually do. The distribution is also unstable: in a synthetic-data control the dominant tensor migrated from x_gate.bias (95% of energy with tp_gate.bias at step 60) to out_norm.weight (57%) by step 400.
divergences.evidence: In-training trace (spy on _AdaptiveSharpnessShift.displace, real pack root data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd): disp#0 [out_norm.weight 0.213, x_gate.bias 0.206, logit_decay 0.152]; disp#69 [copy_transport.log_temp 0.980]; disp#139 [copy_transport.log_temp 0.988]; disp#278 [copy_transport.log_temp 0.998], ||eps||=0.857. Per-tensor table from a second real-data run at step 300: copy_transport.log_temp share=0.9969 rel=4.98e-1; addr_src.weight share=2.31e-06 rel=2.83e-4; tp_out.weight share=5.28e-08 rel=2.62e-5.

divergences.claim: "So swapping r18 -> r3 is a strict superset of what the parent's head could have contributed, in both the disabled and the enabled case." Supported by "[r18's head] is switched off entirely unless the net exposes transition_from_emb … It contributes nothing at eval under any circumstances."
divergences.what_the_code_does: r23_dual_address_transport_pointer inherits transition_from_emb from R18PathStateLatentTransition (MRO: R23 -> R22PrefixContentXAttention -> R18PathStateLatentTransition), and `callable(net.transition_from_emb)` is True — so the parent's head was ENABLED, not disabled. Both heads supervise the same operator with cosine+MSE, but r3's term is a different supervision, not a superset: r18 mines path-similarity triples (path_thresh 0.60) with a change-floor and importance weights, up to 512 examples, weighted 1.0*(0.10*cos + 0.02*mse); r3 mines duplicate-observation triples via a squared-distance clustering rule, up to 192 examples, unweighted, at 0.5*(1.0*cos + 0.05*mse) — a 5x heavier cosine on a differently-selected set. The swap replaces r18's supervision signal; it does not contain it.
divergences.evidence: type(net).__mro__ shows R18PathStateLatentTransition in the chain and `has transition_from_emb: True`; r18 head aux_loss lines 112-170 vs r3 head aux_loss lines 323-334 (`op(pre, cmd_k)` in both, different miners and weights).

divergences.claim: "Spectral cap targets. (D,D) = (768,768) params are r23's tp_out.weight only; r3's head adds no (D,D) matrix … So the cap means the same thing it meant for the parent."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The cap set on this genome is THREE tensors, not one: tr_read.weight, x_out.weight and tp_out.weight are all (768,768) and all routed into _SpectralCap. The conclusion still holds — the head swap adds no (D,D) matrix, so the cap set is identical to the parent's — but the stated inventory is wrong, which matters because the author presents it as a hand-verified static check.
divergences.evidence: Executed the genome's builder+wrap and applied the impl's own filter: dd (spectral cap) = ['tr_read.weight', 'x_out.weight', 'tp_out.weight'].

divergences.claim: "Cost. The added optimizer work is O(#params) elementwise per step plus one scalar device-to-host sync for the global norm — the same order as the spectral cap's existing per-step sync."
divergences.what_the_code_does: `displace` calls `torch.isfinite(g).all()` for every parameter tensor and `torch.isfinite(e).all()` for every staged tensor, each of which forces a host sync — ~284 syncs/step for this net's 142 parameter tensors, versus the parent's ~13 (10 Muon params + 3 spectral-cap params). Measured on CPU with the real net, the optimizer step went from 16.06 ms (parent) to 47.49 ms (new), a 3.0x increase and +31 ms/step — i.e. the "added" work costs about twice the entire pre-existing optimizer, not the same order as one sync. This affects wall-clock/budget only; the step count is fixed so it cannot affect the score.
divergences.evidence: 400-step timing loop on the built genome net: `parent fwd+bwd 18.12s opt 6.42s opt/step 16.06 ms` vs `new fwd+bwd 16.72s opt 18.99s opt/step 47.49 ms`.
